Hello, I’m glad you’re here. I’m [Name], a perinatal mental-health clinician. Over the next few minutes I’d like to use a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—or EPDS—to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. It’s simply ten questions about the past week, and it helps us spot signs of depression or anxiety that can show up after childbirth. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone is in danger. There are no right or wrong answers, and we’ll go at your pace. Ready to start?

In the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?
I’ve still been able to laugh—like when my little one makes those silly milk-drunk faces. It hasn’t felt difficult at all; I actually enjoy those light moments.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, that’s me—I’ve definitely still been able to laugh and see the funny side of things.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

I’ve only blamed myself a little, but it doesn’t stick—like if the baby spits up right after I change her, I might think “oops, maybe I jostled her too much,” but then I shrug it off and move on. It’s not something I dwell on.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason
I’ve been a little anxious, but it’s usually tied to something specific—like wondering if her sniffles mean she’s getting sick. It’s not constant and it doesn’t feel out of nowhere.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
No, I haven’t felt scared or panicky. Sometimes I get a tiny rush of “what if I drop her?” when I’m walking down the stairs, but it’s fleeting—not a real panic.
Things have been getting on top of me
A couple of times, maybe—like yesterday when she wouldn’t nap and the laundry pile felt huge. I just took a breath, put her in the wrap, and chipped away at it. It passed quickly.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, I’ve slept pretty well—she gives me one good four-hour stretch most nights, so I’ve been fine.
I have felt sad or miserable
No, not really. I’m tired sometimes, but I wouldn’t call it sad or miserable—just normal new-mom stuff.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
I haven’t cried at all this week—maybe just one teary moment when she smiled at me, but that was happy tears, not unhappy ones.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, that thought hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 3: Postpartum Depression Screening – Brief Summary

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Occasional situational worry (baby’s health, stairs) – not pervasive  
- Mild, transient “overwhelm” when baby skips nap; resolves quickly  
- Minimal, brief self-blame that does not linger  

**Symptoms denied**  
- Loss of pleasure or laughter  
- Persistent low mood, crying spells, sleep disruption linked to mood, panic, guilt, or self-harm thoughts  

**Pattern**  
No consistent signs of depressive or anxiety disorders; affect appears euthymic and coping skills intact.  

**Risk factors present**  
- Mild situational anxiety (normal newborn vigilance)  
- Infrequent, quickly resolved stress (“getting on top of me”)  

**Safety**  
No self-harm ideation reported; no additional red flags identified.  

**Screening impression**  
Current responses do not indicate elevated risk for postpartum depression or anxiety; routine monitoring and supportive education recommended.
